Dana Nessel — Your Answer Is Required

Attorney General Nessel, the following is addressed directly to you and your office:

MCL 750.539cIdentity fraudBanks uses “J.D., Ph.D.” in professional settings — J.D. not confirmed by any bar

What You Were Told

Your office received the full evidence package — the same 243-page federal master packet delivered to FBI, DOJ, IRS-CI, ED-OIG, HHS-OIG, FinCEN, FTC, and USED.

It contains:

  • Banks’ complete ICHAT criminal record (SID 2029469K) — 9 convictions
  • Holland’s ICHAT and MDOC records (SID 2321035P, MDOC #443789) — drug delivery conviction
  • Holland’s 5 bankruptcy filings with asset concealment evidence
  • LARA entity filings for all Banks-controlled entities (12 total)
  • Wayne County ROD property records showing shared addresses
  • Campaign finance violations and $14,500+ in unpaid fines
  • PCA Management Agreement with false “No Related Parties” representation
  • 72.67% revenue extraction through single-member LLC
  • Board composition: your own AAG sitting as Vice Chair

What Your Office Said

NOTHING.

Not “we’re looking into it.” Not “this falls outside our jurisdiction.” Not “please file through the proper channel.” Not “we have forwarded your complaint.”

Nothing.

What You Already Knew

When Kevin Mok sent the evidence to your office, you already knew that your Assistant Attorney General — Lamar Moreland — sat on the board of Purpose Charter Academy as Vice Chair.

You knew because:

  1. Moreland’s position is public — listed on purposecharteracademy.com/boardofdirectors
  2. Moreland lists it on his LinkedIn — “Board Member” alongside “Assistant Attorney General”
  3. Your office has disclosure requirements — outside employment and board positions must be disclosed

Kevin did NOT know about Moreland when he first contacted your office. He discovered it later, from PCA’s own website.

You knew first. You said nothing. That is not negligence. That is a choice.

Lamar Moreland — Your Answer Is Required

Mr. Moreland, the following is addressed directly to you:

The Question

You are an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Michigan. Your employer — the AG’s office — has jurisdiction over nonprofit fraud, consumer protection, RICO, and charitable trust oversight.

You simultaneously serve as Vice Chair of Purpose Charter Academy — a school:

  • Founded by a man with 9 criminal convictions
  • With 3% math proficiency
  • Where 72.67% of revenue flows to a private LLC controlled by one person
  • Where the foundation’s only financial officers are two convicted felons
  • Where the PAC has $14,500+ in unpaid fines
  • Where the superintendent claims a J.D. not confirmed by any bar

Did you disclose this board position to the AG’s office?

Did the AG’s office approve it?

When a citizen filed a complaint about Banks with the AG’s office, did you recuse yourself?

Did you inform anyone in the AG’s office that the subject of the complaint was the school where you serve as Vice Chair?

Or did the complaint simply… disappear?

Your Candidacy

You are running for 32A District Court Judge — which covers Harper Woods, the jurisdiction where Banks’ home court sits.

If elected, you would be a judge in the same jurisdiction where Banks lives. You would have served on Banks’ school board. You would have been an AAG in the office that should have investigated Banks.

How many positions in Banks’ orbit can one person hold?

The Structure

This is not personal corruption. This is structural capture. One person can simultaneously:

  • Work for the office that investigates charter fraud
  • Govern the school that commits it
  • Run for judge in the jurisdiction where the operator lives

And no rule, no ethics board, no disclosure requirement stopped it.

Renae Moore — Your Answer Is Required

Ms. Moore, the following is addressed directly to you:

You manage 80+ political nonprofit accounts for Michigan’s political class. You are the Treasurer of the Dykema Gossett Federal PAC. You were the Asst. Secretary/Treasurer of both Chatfield’s Peninsula Fund AND Nessel’s Promise to the People Fund.

You testified under oath that you have “no duty to report” questionable spending.

You were wrong. Four bodies of law say you had a duty:

  1. MCL 450.2541 — Michigan nonprofit officer fiduciary duty
  2. 11 CFR 104.14(d) — FEC PAC treasurer personal liability
  3. IRC § 501(c)(4), § 4958 — IRS excess benefit penalties
  4. Common law fiduciary duty — care, loyalty, obedience

But here is the real question:

You manage 80+ accounts. How many of them have the same pattern as the Peninsula Fund? How many have “questionable” expenses you flagged with a policy manual and then watched get violated?

If Banks’ enterprise — Purpose Foundation, Bank on Banks PAC — ran through your desk, did you flag the convicted drug dealer serving as treasurer and secretary?

If not — why not?

If it didn’t run through your desk — whose desk did it run through?

W. Alan Wilk — Your Answer Is Required

Mr. Wilk, the following is addressed directly to you:

You have formed at least 8 dark money 501(c)(4) entities in Michigan, all registered at Dykema’s Lansing office. They accept unlimited anonymous donations and spend unlimited amounts on political advertising.

You are a member of the Republican National Lawyers Association. You were counsel to Governor Engler. You worked on Bush 2000 and 2004 campaigns.

Yet your entities support Democrats (Duggan, Onwenu) and Republicans alike. The ideology doesn’t matter — the structure does. You form the vehicles. Moore manages them. The politicians use them. The donors stay hidden.

Did any entity you formed interact with Brian Banks, Joseph Holland Jr., Purpose Charter Academy, or the Bank on Banks PAC?

Did Save Detroit Jobs or any Wilk-formed entity contribute to or coordinate with Banks’ political campaigns?

How many of your 8+ entities are currently active and accepting donations?

The Proof of Complicity — The Structure

Complicity doesn’t require a conspiracy. It requires structure.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              THE COMPLICITY STRUCTURE                │
│                                                     │
│  Citizen files complaint about Banks                │

│  RESULT: The person who complained is in LEIN.      │
│  The person who was complained about is free.       │
│  The AG's employee is still on the board.           │
│  And nothing changed.                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

This is not one bad actor. This is a system where:

  • The AG can’t investigate because her employee governs the school
  • The desk can’t report because “no duty to report”
  • The lobby can’t allow oversight because Walton paid $4.8M to prevent it
  • The court can’t check because 7 of Banks’ judges sit across 4 courts
  • The school board can’t flag it because the board IS the capture
  • The SBE can’t act because 7 of 8 members chose silence
  • The AG leaves office in 74 days and the next AG inherits all of it

They were already captured before Kevin filed his first complaint. The complaint didn’t fail because it was wrong. It failed because the system it was filed into was the system being complained about.

Can They Ignore This Now?

The question is not whether you CAN ignore this. The question is whether the record will show that you DID.

The 9-Line

The signal format is GTA 08-01-004 MEDEVAC — the military standard for calling in a medical evacuation. You use it when someone is bleeding and the bird needs to get in the air. The format forces structured, unambiguous communication:

Operating 2 charter schools. ~400 children per year. 97% not proficient in math. His LLC takes 72.67% of $4.9M/year in public funds.

Verify: Michigan ICHAT — Search: Brian Roderick Banks. It takes fifteen seconds.

I. Federal Signal — 243-Page Packet to 8 Agencies (Sep 21–25, 2026)

Every agency below received the same 243-page evidence package: criminal history, entity structure, financial self-dealing, judicial connections, BMF lineage, campaign finance violations, RICO predicate acts.

IV. The Mathematics of Silence

Tit for Tat — Axelrod’s Tournament

In Robert Axelrod’s iterated prisoner’s dilemma tournament (1984), the winning strategy is Tit for Tat:

  1. Start by cooperating. Always.
  2. Mirror what the other player does. If they cooperate, cooperate. If they defect, defect.
  3. Forgive immediately. If they return to cooperation, you return to cooperation.

Kevin cooperated first. Every signal was cooperation — using lawful channels, providing evidence, offering to work together (“I am not your enemy”), providing contact information, waiting for response.

The institutions defected. Not by attacking — by choosing SILENCE.

Null ≠ Parasite… Until It Does

In biology, null means UNKNOWN — default to cooperation. A commensal takes without harming. A mutualist gives back.

But there is a threshold. When signal has been sent through EVERY lawful channel, to EVERY oversight body, with 243 pages of evidence, and the response is NULL across every channel — null becomes data.

VIII. To the People Reading This in Silence

entry.title: Institutional Response Tracker
entry.content:
From Courts to Checkpoints

The Anderson Localization analysis showed that captured judges create disorder in the judicial lattice. Cases that enter cannot propagate to a fair hearing.

But courts are not the only institutional checkpoint. Michigan has layered accountability structures: credentialing bodies, oversight commissions, authorizers, professional discipline departments, and law enforcement agencies. Each exists to catch what the others miss.

The question this page answers: When the same verified evidence is submitted to multiple institutional checkpoints simultaneously, which ones act and which ones don’t?

The answer reveals whether the accountability system functions or whether the disorder extends beyond the courts into the institutions designed to oversee them.

The Model

Every institutional checkpoint is a lattice site. Evidence arrives like an electron. Either the institution transmits it forward (investigation, action, referral) or it absorbs and traps it (closure, dismissal, non-response).

If every checkpoint absorbs, the system is fully localized. No accountability can propagate.

The measurement is simple:

InputWhat Was Submitted
SubjectBrian Roderick Banks: 9 criminal convictions (SID 2029469K), unauthorized use of “J.D.” credential, operation of two DPSCD-authorized charter schools
EvidenceICHAT criminal record, LARA corporate filings, MOECS credential audit, academic performance data (3% math proficiency), financial records ($4.9M revenue, 72.67% extraction to Purpose Group LLC), campaign finance data
FormatVerified public records, structured for independent verification
Sitedetroit.primals.eco

The same evidence package. Multiple institutions. Measure the output.

The Data

Checkpoint Response Table

This table is updated as responses arrive. Each row documents the institutional output for the same evidentiary input.

#InstitutionDepartmentFiledResponseDaysResult
1Michigan Dept. of EducationEducator Excellence20222022–Cleared with conditions
2Detroit Public Schools CDBoard of DirectorsJul 2025Jul 2025–Authorized second school
3State Bar of MichiganUPL Dept. (File 26-UP-51)Aug 2026Sep 30, 2026~30Administratively closed
4State Bar of MichiganUPL (2nd complaint)Sep 2026–PendingAwaiting response
5Baker CollegeHuman ResourcesOct 2026Oct 5, 2026<2Permanently severed
6Attorney Grievance CommissionProfessional discipline (x7)Sep-Oct 2026–PendingInvestigations pending
7Judicial Tenure CommissionJudicial conductSep 2026Sep 2026~5Investigations opened
8Central Michigan UniversityCharter authorizationPending––Notification staged
9MDE (Round 2)Credential re-examinationPending––Notification staged
10Detroit Inspector GeneralMunicipal oversightPending––Complaint staged

Key Observations

The only institution that acted in under 48 hours was a private employer with no regulatory obligation.

Baker College reviewed the same evidence that Michigan’s credentialing body, authorizing district, and professional bar department reviewed. Baker permanently severed ties. The regulatory bodies either cleared him, authorized him, or closed the complaint.

The UPL Department’s stated reason for closure: “Does not meet the standards set by the Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee to pursue this matter further.” The subject uses “J.D.” in professional communications, holds no bar admission in any jurisdiction, and operates a school named “School for Law and Public Service.”

The UPL Department’s stated alternative: “You may have other remedies available to you.”

The UPL complaint was the first of several submitted as the scope of the unauthorized credential use became clear through the investigation. Additional complaints remain pending and will be updated here as responses arrive.

The Asymmetry

Michigan’s system demands active defense from individuals:

  • A parent must file a motion and appear at a hearing to see their own children
  • A citizen must file an affirmative defense within 14 days to contest a personal protection order
  • A pro se litigant must meet the same procedural standards as a licensed attorney
  • A victim of assault must obtain and serve their own police report
  • A custody case requires the responding parent to affirmatively request the investigation the filing parent opted out of

But when a citizen uses the system’s own accountability tools:

  • A UPL complaint against a 9-time convicted felon using “J.D.” is closed as not meeting standards
  • An administrator certification for a habitual offender is granted with conditions
  • A second charter school is authorized for an operator whose first school ranks in the bottom 3% statewide
  • A police report filed at the scene of an assault requires the victim to drive to the precinct to retrieve it

The system enforces process against citizens aggressively. It declines to enforce against its own members passively.

This asymmetry is not incidental. It is the localization.

When the disorder in the lattice extends from the courts into the oversight bodies, the accountability signal has nowhere to propagate. Every checkpoint absorbs it. The individual is left with “other remedies available to you,” which means: the system has told you it will not help.

The Measurement Continues

This page is a living document. As institutional responses arrive, the table updates. Each response or non-response is a data point in the same experiment.

The question is not whether any single institution failed. Institutions make judgment calls. The question is whether the pattern of non-response across multiple independent checkpoints reveals structural localization rather than individual discretion.

When the same evidence produces action from a private college in 48 hours and produces closure from a state regulatory body in 30 days, the comparison is the finding. No editorial interpretation is required.

This is Anderson Localization measured in institutional responses rather than court assignments. The physics is the same: disorder prevents propagation. The measurement is how deep the disorder goes.
